title: Review Writing — book and film review format
notes: **What it is:** a balanced critical evaluation — what the work is, what it does well, what falls short, and whether it is worth the reader's time.

**Structure:** Title + basic details (title, author/director, year, genre) → Brief SPOILER-FREE summary (2–3 sentences) → Strengths (one concrete example/quote) → Weaknesses (fair, with why it matters) → Recommendation + verdict/rating.

**Review grammar:** present simple dominates ('the story follows…'); evaluative adjectives (compelling, uneven, luminous); concessive fairness ('although the plot is thin, the philosophy is profound'); soft hedging ('readers may find…').
**Never spoil the ending** — restraint reads as mature judgement.
**Full guide:** Full model answers, starting-line banks and exam tips: [/knowledge/writing](/knowledge/writing).

**Review structure (classified)**

| Section | Content | Length share |
|---|---|---|
| Hook + basics | Title, author/director, genre | 10% |
| Summary | Premise, no spoilers | 25% |
| Analysis | Strengths and weaknesses | 40% |
| Verdict | Recommendation + rating | 25% |

**What to judge in a review**

| Criterion | Book | Film |
|---|---|---|
| Story | Plot coherence | Pacing, structure |
| Craft | Prose, voice | Cinematography, editing |
| Characters | Depth, growth | Casting, performance |
| Impact | Ideas that stay | Emotion, rewatch value |

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Review anatomy: title/creator → one-line premise (no spoilers) → two strengths → one weakness → verdict with a rating — the five-part frame.
Trick 2: Judge against PURPOSE, not taste: a thriller must thrill, a documentary must inform — state the criterion before judging.
Trick 3: Use the vocabulary bank: plot, pacing, characterisation, cinematography, narrative arc — technical terms lift the band instantly.
practiceQuestions: Q. Write a short review of a film you have recently watched. (4 marks) — premise, one strength with example, one weakness, verdict.
Q. What must a review avoid? (1 mark) — major spoilers and purely personal bias without criteria.
